title: System Design: Beginner to Advanced
subtitle: From first-principles capacity math to distributed consensus, multi-region reliability, and real-world architecture.
description: A complete beginner-to-advanced path covering requirements, networking, storage internals, caching, replication, sharding, streaming, distributed systems, reliability, security, and 16 production case studies.
audience: Students and early-career developers learning system design from scratch
Software engineers preparing for senior engineering and architecture interviews
Self-directed builders wanting practical labs, animated visuals, and primary sources
prerequisites: Basic programming comfort in any language
Elementary HTTP and database familiarity helpful but not required
outcomes: Convert ambiguous product prompts into measurable functional requirements, SLIs/SLOs, and capacity math
Explain end-to-end internet transport (DNS, TCP, TLS 1.3, HTTP/2-3, CDN, load balancing) and API contracts
Choose and model storage engines (B+Trees, LSM-Trees, SQL, NoSQL, object storage) with transaction guarantees
Design resilient caching, replication, consistent-hash sharding, and asynchronous event pipelines
Reason rigorously about partial failure, clocks, quorums, CAP/PACELC, consensus, overload control, and security
Produce complete System Design Documents, ADRs, load benchmarks, and failure-mode analyses across 16 case studies

downloads.notes: All 40 standalone .html decks preserve step animations, Mermaid diagrams, speaker notes, local webcam bubble, and 40 interactive simulations; PDF and PPTX provide static snapshots.
